text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementAnthropologyWe Now Know What Denisovans Looked LikeAn analysis of their skulls paints a picture of our archaic cousinsJCBy Jake Currie1:00 PM CDT on October 22, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleOf all our ancient relatives, the Denisovans might be the most mysterious. While fossils from these archaic hominins were unearthed nearly half a century ago, they were only determined to be a genetically distinct hominin line in the past 15 years. The name Denisovans comes from the Denisova cave in Russia where some of the first specimens were found. Now a new study published in Nature is putting a face to that name.  Powered By 10 ShareNextStayA team of paleoanthropologists and geneticists from the Chinese Academy of Sciences investigated a cache of 20 fossils dating to around 130,000 years old that were discovered in Xujiayao alongside tools and various animal remains. When the fossils were excavated in the 1970s, it was unclear which hominin group they belonged to.
